```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

require(tidyverse)
require(kableExtra)
require(mirt)
require(mirtCAT)
require(ggpubr)
```

When deciding how to assess bilingual children, researcher now have several options, including:
 - full CDI in each language
 - Swadesh-CDI in each language
 - CDI-CATs (for available languages)
 - published short forms (for available languages)
 - DLL-ES (only for English and Spanish)

The question is: what is the best option (or combination), if the goal is to assess children's ability in each language?
We'll start just by looking at a correlation matrix comparing each measure's estimated ability. 

```{r load-data}
# BiLexPo data -- has 'bilingual' identifier in dataset_origin_name
bi_dat <- readRDS("data/bilingual_item_data_clean.Rds") |>
  filter(dataset_origin_name %in% 
           c("Marchman Dallas Bilingual", "Hoff_English_Mexican_Bilingual")) |>
  filter(production!=0, production!=680) # no floor or ceiling

d_demo <- bi_dat |> select(language, data_id, child_id, dataset_origin_name, form, age, sex, produces) |>
  group_by(language, data_id, child_id, dataset_origin_name, form, age, sex) |>
  summarise(production = sum(produces, na.rm=T))

d_mat <- bi_dat |> pivot_wider(id_cols = data_id, names_from = uni_lemma, values_from = produces) 


dupes <- bi_dat |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), .by = c(data_id, uni_lemma)) |>
  dplyr::filter(n > 1L)
# per-language data -- but how do we identify the bilinguals?
```

```{r load-irt-models}
load("models/eng_ws_wg_mod_2pl_nobad.Rds") # mod_2pl
en_mod <- mod_2pl
load("models/sp_ws_wg_mod_2pl_nobad.Rds")
sp_mod <- mod_2pl

# age-based starting items
en_start_items <- read_csv("models/EN_production_start_items_by_age.csv")
sp_start_items <- read_csv("models/SP_production_start_items_by_age.csv")

preferredCAT <- function(dat, method='ML', min_SEM=.15, start_item=c()) {
  all_items = c() # track freq of all the items that were asked 
  parms = c()
  if(length(start_item)==0) start_item = 'MI' # otherwise supply age-based
  results <- mirtCAT(mo = mod_2pl, criteria = 'MI', start_item = start_item, 
                     method = method, local_pattern = dat, 
                     design = list(min_items = 25,
                                   max_items = 50, 
                                   min_SEM = min_SEM))
  for(s in 1:nrow(dat)) {
    all_items = c(all_items, results[[s]]$items_answered)
    so <- summary(results[[s]])
    parms = rbind(parms, c(t(so$final_estimates), length(so$items_answered)))
  }
  sum_score = rowSums(dat)
  parms = data.frame(cbind(parms, sum_score))
  names(parms) = c("thetaCAT","CAT_SE","Qs_asked","sum_score")
  want = list(all_items=all_items, parms=parms)
  return(want)
}

start_item_subj = rep(NA, nrow(d_demo))
for(i in 1:nrow(d_demo)) {
  start_item_subj[i] = subset(age_startits, age==d_demo[i,]$age)$index
}

cat_result = preferredCAT(d_mat_imp, method='MAP', start_item=start_item_subj)

d_demo$fullCDItheta = fscores_2pl$ability
d_demo$CATtheta = cat_result$parms$thetaCAT
d_demo$CAT_SE = cat_result$parms$CAT_SE
d_demo$Qs_asked = cat_result$parms$Qs_asked
```
